title: A smooth circle map and coordinate-independent rank
promptMarkdown: Let $F:S^1\to S^1$ be $F(x,y)=(x^2-y^2,2xy)$. (a) Show it maps the circle to itself and compute its local expressions in angle charts. (b) Compute its differential on the tangent vector $(-y,x)$ and determine its rank everywhere. Prove why changes of source and target chart cannot change that rank. (c) Determine every fibre and decide whether it is a diffeomorphism. (d) Compare the reasons this map fails to be a diffeomorphism with the map that is the identity from the standard real line to the line charted by $x^3$, and with the line with two origins.
hintLadder: Differentiate the polynomial map on the circle tangent.
Rank is invariant under multiplication by invertible coordinate-change derivatives.
Separate a bijection issue from an inverse-smoothness issue and from a topology axiom.
